sentences: New job? Your first payslip could be almost {£210|two hundred and ten pounds} short.
Blame the tiny code next to your name.
Most people's says {1257L|twelve fifty-seven L} right there.
That's not random: it's your {£12,570|twelve thousand, five hundred and seventy pounds} tax-free.
Without your {P45|P forty-five}, a new boss may use {0T|zero T} instead.
Then not one pound of your pay is tax-free.
Once {HMRC|H M R C} has your details, it comes back in your pay.
So before your next new job, remember:
